Schema validation and structured data handling

Learning how to apply these tools responsibly while maintaining production-quality standards

About QuEra Computing, Inc.
QuEra Computing is building the world’s most powerful neutral-atom quantum computers. Our systems are designed to scale and enable groundbreaking advances in science and technology. We collaborate closely with leading academic and industry partners to push the boundaries of quantum computing, error correction, and fault tolerance.
Summary
QuEra Computing Inc. seeks creative and collaborative Scientific Software Interns to help advance the software that connects high-level quantum applications to neutral-atom quantum computers. Working with software engineers, experimental and computational physicists, and a community of industry and academic collaborators, you will contribute to research and engineering at the intersection of programming languages, compilers, and quantum computing.
We offer a range of research and engineering projects, from investigating new compilation methods and developing prototypes to building software infrastructure and integrating with quantum hardware. Projects span quantum circuits, atom movement, and pulse-level control. Each intern will work with a mentor on a project matched to their interests, experience, and team priorities.
Our compiler stack is evolving from Python toward Rust, creating opportunities to contribute to existing tools, including our open-source compiler framework Kirin, as well as new infrastructure. Depending on the project, your contributions may include algorithms, research findings, benchmarks, or tested and documented software that supports the next generation of neutral-atom quantum computing.
Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and those received before Nov. 15, 2026 are guaranteed full consideration.
Internship terms are flexible, including outside the summer, and can be arranged around candidates’ availability.
Responsibilities
Responsibilities will vary by project and may include:
Investigate research questions in quantum compilation, programming languages, or scientific software; develop prototypes and evaluate approaches through experiments and benchmarks
Develop domain-specific languages, intermediate representations, compiler analyses, and transformations for quantum circuits, atom movement, or pulse-level control
Build and improve compiler infrastructure in Rust or Python, and support integration with quantum hardware platforms
Collaborate with your mentor, software engineers, and physicists to define project goals, discuss technical approaches, and communicate results
Contribute tests, documentation, and reproducible examples or experiments appropriate to your project
Qualifications
Experience programming in Python, Rust, or another relevant language, and willingness to learn the tools needed for your project
A foundation in computer science or computational methods, demonstrated through coursework, research, personal projects, or other relevant experience
Interest in research, software engineering, or both, applied to compilers and scientific software for quantum computing
Ability to approach technical problems systematically and communicate ideas, questions, and results clearly
Enthusiasm for collaborative work and for building tools used by researchers and developers
Preferred Qualifications
The following backgrounds are relevant to different projects; applicants are not expected to have experience in all of them:
Academic training or research in computer science, physics, applied mathematics, or a related field
Experience with compiler development, intermediate representations such as Static Single Assignment (SSA), program analysis, or optimization
Knowledge of programming language design, type systems, or programming language theory
Experience with Rust, systems programming, or Python-based scientific software
Experience designing experiments, evaluating algorithms, or developing reproducible benchmarks
Familiarity with quantum computing, quantum error correction, or atomic, molecular, and optical (AMO) physics
Experience with version control, code review, testing, debugging, profiling, or contributions to open-source projects
Why Join QuEra?
You will be part of a collaborative, fast-moving team at the forefront of quantum technology. This internship offers exposure to both cutting-edge theory and practical implementation, with opportunities to contribute to peer-reviewed research and real-world quantum hardware development.

Dyna Robotics
builds general-purpose robots powered by a proprietary embodied AI foundation model with top-in-industry generalization and real-world performance. Already deployed with customers across multiple industries, our robots do commercial-grade work in the physical world. Our team comes from Google DeepMind, Meta, and Cruise, and we're backed by CRV, First Round, and other leading investors.
The Role
Dyna's robots only create value when they're reliably connected. Robotics isn't like typical enterprise software: latency that an ordinary business app would shrug off turns teleoperation and remote supervision into jerky, unsafe, or outright failed robot behavior. A degraded link here isn't a background IT ticket: it can be the difference between a robot finishing a task and stalling mid-motion. This role owns the technical side of network performance in two settings: making sure a demo never drops mid-pitch, and making sure a deployed robot stays online, monitorable, and controllable on network infrastructure Dyna doesn't own or control. This is a build role, not a network-admin or support role: you'll design and build the systems (monitoring, automated failover, self-healing diagnostics) that make connectivity reliable by default, so stability is a property of the system rather than something a person has to catch and fix after it breaks.
What You'll Do
Own network performance for remote teleoperation.
Measure and minimize end-to-end latency and jitter, tune how video and control streams are transported and prioritized, and make sure sessions degrade gracefully (lower bitrate, prioritized control traffic, safe fallback behavior) instead of failing when the link gets worse. A reliable, low-latency link is what keeps a human safely in the loop.
Build the fleet connectivity stack.
Monitoring, diagnostics, and automated failover software that keeps every robot's connection healthy in production, turning a dropped connection into an automatic root cause and recovery, not a 2am page to go run tcpdump on-site.
Own the network side of site bring-up.
Build tooling that assesses a customer's network before a robot ever arrives, then work with the deployment team to configure the right failover, QoS, and VPN setup for that site.
Design connectivity for real-world chaos:
warehouse WiFi dead zones, cellular failover, and VPN-gated corporate networks with firewall rules you can't change.
Diagnose field issues on networks you don't control,
then build the fix so the same failure never happens twice.
Make the office and demo network rock-solid by default,
so a live demo never drops in front of a customer or investor.
Partner with engineers and researchers
to keep the network ahead of what they need for training-data upload and live model debugging.
Be the person in the room
when connectivity is on the line, whether that's a live demo or a field incident.
What You'll Bring
Hands-on experience debugging real-world networks: WiFi/RF troubleshooting and packet-level diagnostics (Wireshark, tcpdump, iperf)
Deep understanding of TCP, UDP, and how they behave on lossy, high-jitter links, plus strong Linux networking skills (routing, traffic shaping with tc, firewalling, VPNs such as WireGuard)
A track record of shipping production-quality software in C++, Rust, or Python, not just scripts and prototypes
Comfort working in the field and communicating clearly under pressure: you'll be translating failures into fixes mid-demo and mid-deployment
Degree in CS, EE, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience
Strongly Preferred
Experience with real-time media or low-latency transport: WebRTC, RTP, adaptive bitrate, congestion control, jitter buffers, or UDP-based protocols like QUIC or SRT
Experience managing connectivity for a fleet of edge devices (robots, vehicles, IoT) deployed on networks you don't own
Hands-on work with cellular/LTE/5G failover hardware, link bonding, or multipath networking
Bonus Points For
Experience with pub/sub or messaging middleware (ZeroMQ, ROS 2, DDS, or similar), especially running it over WiFi or WAN links
Experience with network hardware: managed switches, access points, mesh networking, cellular routers
Experience supporting live events, demos, or on-site customer deployments where network reliability was your responsibility
At
Dyna Robotics
, we build technology for the real world, which requires a team as diverse as the environments our robots inhabit. We are an equal opportunity employer committed to technical rigor and mutual respect.
Don’t let a checklist stop you.
Data shows that underrepresented groups often only apply if they meet 100% of the criteria. We value problem-solving and grit over keyword matching. If you’re passionate about robotics, no matter your discipline, we want to hear from you, even if you don't check every box.
